  "text": "The kitchen floor was dry when they came back, though Mara’s shoes left wet prints across it. Her mother stood by the table, holding three towels. She gave one to Mara, one to her sister, and hesitated over the third.

The child took it. Up close, she looked less like Mara than she had from the doorway. She had a chipped front tooth and a narrow scar beneath her chin. Mara remembered falling from the harbor wall, remembered her sister pressing a cloth to the cut.

“I thought you were gone,” her mother whispered.

Her sister shook her head. “I was here.”

Mara looked at the door. It had shrunk to its usual size, a little cupboard beneath the sink. Inside were a mop, a tin of polish, and the shell the child had carried. Mara picked it up. She heard no sea in it, only her own breathing.

The harbor master knocked once from the other side of the cupboard. Then his footsteps faded.

Their mother pulled out a chair for the child. No one knew whether to ask her what she wanted, or how long she would stay. At last Mara set a glass of water before her.

The child drank half and pushed the rest toward Mara. It was something her sister had always done when they were small, insisting that a shared glass tasted colder.

Mara drank. Across the table, her sister smiled at the child, then at her. Their mother sat down beside them, still clutching the unused towel."
